notes: Pilot only. No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional — not absolute anatomy. No Travell verbatim text.

relations.clinical_context: Knee pain with limited local knee findings, especially in children/adolescents or when hip ROM reproduces familiar knee pain.
supporting_evidence: Hip pathology presenting as knee pain is a classic clinical pitfall
Negative meniscal/ligament tests do not locate the source to the knee

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Clinical pattern — no invented numeric accuracy.

limitations: Adults can also have dual hip–knee OA patterns
Do not skip local knee exam
alternative_explanations: Lumbar referral (less common for isolated anterior knee)
recommended_examination: Hip ROM + FADIR when knee exam is incongruent
Standard knee cluster for mechanism-based suspicion
Red flags for infection / tumor if night pain systemic
red_flags: Child with knee pain — always screen hip (SCFE / Perthes pathways)
Unable to bear weight after trauma

references.citation: Kocher MS / pediatric hip–knee pain clinical teaching literature — SCFE presenting as knee pain (clinical caution).
Reiman MP et al. Hip examination reviews — referred pain considerations.

relations.clinical_context: Twist injury or mechanical symptoms; McMurray negative or equivocal.
supporting_evidence: Meniscal special tests have limited standalone accuracy in systematic reviews
Clusters (history + joint-line tenderness + composite tests) preferred

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp. Negative McMurray ≠ meniscus cleared.

recommended_examination: Joint-line tenderness + Thessaly / squat as adjuncts
Imaging if management depends on it
red_flags: Locked knee with true mechanical block — urgent pathway

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Physical examination tests of the knee / meniscus — systematic reviews with cautious interpretation.
Solomon DH et al. Does this patient have a torn meniscus or ligament of the knee? JAMA Rational Clinical Examination.

relations.clinical_context: Suspected meniscal pathology; Thessaly negative or not tolerated.
supporting_evidence: Early promising accuracy reports were not consistently replicated — treat as mixed

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Replication concerns; never invent numeric values from memory.

recommended_examination: Do not auto-attribute to 'muscle' because Thessaly is negative

references.citation: Meniscal clinical test literature including Thessaly replication/critique discussions in sports medicine reviews (qualitative mixed evidence).
Hegedus EJ et al. Knee exam systematic reviews.

relations.clinical_context: Pivot trauma or giving-way; Lachman negative or equivocal — especially acute hemarthrosis / guard.
supporting_evidence: Lachman is among the better ACL clinical tests but remains imperfect
Examiner experience and patient guarding matter

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Qualitative: better than many knee tests for ACL, still not perfect exclusion. No invented LR−.

recommended_examination: Pivot shift / anterior drawer as adjuncts when tolerable
MRI when clinical uncertainty and management depends on it
red_flags: Multi-ligament / dislocation suspicion — vascular/neuro emergency pathway

references.citation: Benjaminse A et al. Clinical diagnosis of an anterior cruciate ligament rupture: a meta-analysis. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther.
Solomon DH et al. JAMA Rational Clinical Examination — knee ligaments.

relations.clinical_context: Anterior knee pain with stairs/sitting plus possible joint-line or degenerative features.
supporting_evidence: PFPS is a clinical diagnosis of exclusion/pattern; OA and meniscal changes can coexist on imaging without explaining all symptoms

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Pattern-based — avoid structural over-attribution from imaging alone.

limitations: Do not chase every meniscal signal in middle-aged anterior pain
recommended_examination: Load/aggravating factor analysis (stairs, squat, prolonged flexion)
Hip and foot kinetic contributors as hypotheses

references.citation: Willy RW et al. Patellofemoral Pain CPG. JOSPT.
Crossley KM et al. 2016 Patellofemoral pain consensus statement from the 4th International Patellofemoral Pain Research Retreat. BJSM.
